questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with speed 20 m s$^{-1}$ from a point $A$, which is $h$ metres above the ground. The ball moves freely under gravity until it hits the ground 5 s later.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Use of $s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2$ to find $h$. Must quote the correct formula and be using 20 & 5, but condone slips in substitution. Accept complete alternative solutions working via the maximum height (max ht 20.4..., time to top 2.04...). Accept complete alternative methods using other suvat equations.
A1: Correctly substituted equation(s). Condone use of a premature approximation.
A1: $h=22.5$. Accept 22.5 or 23. Maximum 3sf. $-22.5$ is A0.
NB Do not ignore subsequent working if they reach 22.5 and then move on to do further work.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $h=-20\times 5+\frac{1}{2}\times 9.8\times 25$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A second ball is thrown vertically downwards with speed $w$ m s$^{-1}$ from $A$ and moves freely under gravity until it hits the ground.

The first ball hits the ground with speed $V$ m s$^{-1}$ and the second ball hits the ground with speed $\frac{3}{4}V$ m s$^{-1}$.

(b) Find the value of $w$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) First ball - M1: use of suvat to find $V$ or $V^2$. Follow their $h$.
A1: $V^2=20^2+2\times 9.8\times 22.5$ ($V^2=841$), $V=29$. Correct only (condone $-29$).
Second ball - M1: suvat equation in $V$ (or their $V$) to find $w$. Must be using the $\frac{3}{4}$.
A1ft: Correctly substituted equation with their $V$ and their $h$: $\left(\frac{3}{4}V\right)^2=w^2+2\times 9.8\times 22.5$, giving $w^2=\frac{9}{16}\times 841-2\times 9.8\times 22.5$.
A1: $w=5.66$ or 5.7. Answer correct to 2 s.f. or to 3 s.f.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- OR $V=-20+(5\times 9.8)$ $=29$

questions.stem: A particle $P$ of mass 1.5 kg is placed at a point $A$ on a rough plane which is inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is 0.6

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $P$ rests in equilibrium at $A$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: For resolution of forces parallel or perpendicular to the plane. Weight must be resolved. Condone sin/cos confusion.
A1: $R(\perp\text{plane})$ $N=1.5g\cos30$. Correct equation for $N$ (12.7).
A1: $R(\parallel\text{plane})$ $F=1.5g\cos60$. Correct equation for $F$ (7.35). Condone $\mu R$.
M1: Use of $F_{\max}=\mu N$ and compare with $F$, or find the value of their $\frac{F}{N}$ and compare with $\mu$: $\frac{F}{N}=\frac{\cos60}{\cos30}=0.577...<0.6$
A1: $\therefore$ equilibrium. Reach given conclusion correctly. They must make some comment, however brief.
ALT for first 3 marks: Resolve vertically $N\cos30+F\cos60=1.5g$ (M1A1); Resolve horizontally $N\cos60=F\cos30$ (A1).
ALT for last 2 marks: $F_{\max}=0.6\times12.73=7.63>7.35$ (M1); $\therefore P$ is at rest (A1).
If the candidate has given the equation of motion for the particle moving down the plane then A1 for $1.5g\sin30-\mu R=\pm1.5a$. To score more they need to comment correctly on their answer: $a=-0.19$ impossible (M1); Conclude that the particle cannot be moving (A1).
Candidates who think that the diagram applies to (a) will score nothing in (a) but if they carry their results forward in to (b) then their work can score the marks available in (b).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A horizontal force of magnitude $X$ newtons is now applied to $P$, as shown in Figure 1. The force acts in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope of the inclined plane.

The particle is on the point of moving up the plane.

(b) Find
(i) the magnitude of the normal reaction of the plane on $P$,
(ii) the value of $X$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $R(\perp\text{plane})$ $N=1.5g\cos30+X\cos60$. Requires all 3 terms. Condone sin/cos confusion and sign errors.
M1: $R(\parallel\text{plane})$ $X\cos30=1.5g\cos60+F$. Requires all 3 terms. Condone sin/cos confusion and sign errors.
A1: Both equations correct unsimplified.
DM1: Use $F=0.6N$ to form an equation in $N$ or in $X$: $N=1.5g\cos30+\frac{\cos60}{\cos30}(1.5g\cos60+0.6N)$, giving $N\left(1-\frac{\cos60}{\cos30}\times0.6\right)=1.5g\cos30+\frac{\cos60}{\cos30}\times1.5g\cos60$. Dependent on the two previous M marks. OR: $0.6(X\cos60+1.5g\cos30)+1.5g\sin30=X\cos30$
A1: (i) $N=26$ or 26.0 (N). First value found correctly (N or X).
DM1: Substitute their $N$ (or $X$) to find $X$ (or $N$): $X=(N-1.5g\cos30)\div\cos60$. Dependent on the previous M mark.
A1: (ii) $X=26$ or $26.5$. Second value found correctly.
Alt: Resolve vertically $N\cos30-F\cos60=1.5g$, $N\cos30-0.6N\cos60=1.5g$ (M1, DM1); Use $F=0.6N$ (A1); $N=\frac{1.5g}{\cos30-0.6\cos60}=26$ or 26.0 (A1); Resolve horizontally, follow their $N$. Must have all terms. Condone sin/cos confusion. $X=F\cos30+N\cos60=N(0.6\cos30+\cos60)$ (M1, DM1); $X=26$ or 26.5 (A1). Substitute for $F$ and $N$.

questions.stem: A plank $AB$, of length 6 m and mass 4 kg, rests in equilibrium horizontally on two supports at $C$ and $D$, where $AC=2$ m and $DB=1$ m. A brick of mass 2 kg rests on the plank at $A$ and a brick of mass 3 kg rests on the plank at $B$, as shown in Figure 2. The plank is modelled as a uniform rod and all bricks are modelled as particles.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the magnitude of the reaction exerted on the plank
(i) by the support at $C$,
(ii) by the support at $D$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a)(i) M(D): $3R_C+1\times3g=2\times4g+5\times2g$. Requires all 4 terms of the correct form, but condone sign errors. $1\times$ need not be seen. Correct unsimplified equation (M1, A1). $R_C=5g$ or 49 N (A1).
(ii) $R(\uparrow)$: $R_C+R_D=4g+2g+3g$, requires all 5 terms. Correct unsimplified equation (M1, A1). $R_D=4g$ or 39 or 39.2N (A1).
Alt: M(A): $3\times4g+6\times3g=2R_C+5R_D (=30g)$ (M1A1). M(B): $3\times4g+6\times2g=R_D+4R_C (=24g)$ (M1A1). M(C): $3R_D+2\times2g=1\times4g+4\times3g$. M(centre): $3g\times3+R_C=2R_D+2g\times3$. Solve simultaneously for $R_C$ and $R_D$: $R_C=5g$ or 49 N, $R_D=4g$ or 39 or 39.2N (A1, A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The 3 kg brick is now removed and replaced with a brick of mass $x$ kg at $B$. The plank remains horizontal and in equilibrium but the reactions on the plank at $C$ and at $D$ now have equal magnitude.

(b) Find the value of $x$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M(D): $3R_C+xg=8g+10g$ ($3R_C=(18-x)g$) (M1: first equation in $x$ and $R$ (or $R_C$ and $R_D$) - correct terms required but condone sign slips). $R(\uparrow)$: $R_C+R_D=4g+2g+xg$ (M1: a second equation, correct terms required but condone sign slips). Alternatives: M(B): $4R_C+R_D=12g+12g$; M(A): $2R_C+5R_D=6xg+3\times4g$; M(C): $2\times2g+3R_D=4xg+1\times4g$.
DM1: Use $R_C=R_D$ and solve for $x$ (as far as $x=...$). Dependent on the two previous M marks: $2(18-x)g=3(6+x)g$.
A1: $x=3.6$

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors due east and due north respectively. Position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]

A boy $B$ is running in a field with constant velocity $(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$. At time $t=0$, $B$ is at the point with position vector $10\mathbf{j}$ m.

Find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Use Pythagoras: Speed $=\sqrt{3^2+(-2)^2}$ or $\sqrt{3^2+2^2}$.
A1: $=\sqrt{13}$ m s$^{-1}$. Accept 3.6 or better. Ignore their diagram if it does not support their working.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the direction in which $B$ is running, giving your answer as a bearing.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Find a relevant angle: $\tan\theta=\frac{2}{3}$, $\theta=33.7$ OR $\tan\theta=\frac{3}{2}$, $\theta=56.3$ OR find another useful angle.
A1: Their angle correct (seen or implied).
A1: Bearing $=124$. Correct bearing. Accept $124^\circ$ or awrt $124/124^\circ$. Accept N 124 E or S 56 E.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At time $t=0$, a girl $G$ is at the point with position vector $(4\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$ m. The girl is running with constant velocity $\left(\frac{5}{3}\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}\right)$ m s$^{-1}$ and meets $B$ at the point $P$.

(c) Find
(i) the value of $t$ when they meet,
(ii) the position vector of $P$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Find the position vector of $B$ or $G$ at time $t$.
A1: Correct for $B$: $\mathbf{r}_B=10\mathbf{j}+t(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$.
A1: Correct for $G$: $\mathbf{r}_G=4\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+t\left(\frac{5}{3}\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}\right)$.
DM1: Compare coefficients of $\mathbf{i}$ or of $\mathbf{j}$ to form an equation in $t$: $3t=4+\frac{5}{3}t$ OR $10-2t=-2+2t$.
A1: (i) $t=3$ s. Correct unambiguous conclusion.
A1: (ii) $\mathbf{r}=10\mathbf{j}+3(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})=(9\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ m OR $\mathbf{r}=4\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+3\left(\frac{5}{3}\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}\right)=(9\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j})$ m. Final answer. Accept with no units. Do not ignore subsequent working.

questions.stem: A car starts from rest at a point $A$ and moves along a straight horizontal road. The car moves with constant acceleration 1.5 m s$^{-2}$ for the first 8 s. The car then moves with constant acceleration 0.8 m s$^{-2}$ for the next 20 s. It then moves with constant speed for $T$ seconds before slowing down with constant deceleration 2.8 m s$^{-2}$ until it stops at a point $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the speed of the car 28 s after leaving $A$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Use of $v=u+at$ or equivalent for $t=8$: $v_1=8\times1.5(=12)$.
M1: Follow their 12: $v_2=12+0.8\times20$.
A1: $v_2=28$ m s$^{-1}$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Sketch, in the space provided, a speed–time graph to illustrate the motion of the car as it travels from $A$ to $B$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: shape.
B1ft: nos: 8, 28; 12, 28 indicated. Follow their 12, 28.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the distance travelled by the car during the first 28 s of its journey from $A$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Correct method for distance for the triangle (0-8) or the trapezium (8-28).
A1ft: first 8 s: dist $=\frac{1}{2}\times8\times12$ ($=48$). Follow their 12.
A1ft: next 20 s: dist $=\frac{1}{2}\times(12+28)\times20$ ($=400$). Follow their 12, 28.
A1: Total dist $=448$ m. Correct answer only (cao).

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The distance from $A$ to $B$ is 2 km.

(d) Find the value of $T$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: Find area of right hand triangle or an expression in $T$ for the trapezium (rectangle + triangle): $0=28^2-2\times2.8s$.
A1ft: $s=\frac{28^2}{2\times2.8}(=140)$. Follow their 28.
DM1: Form an equation in $T$ for their 16, 448 and 140: $448+140+28T=2000$. Dependent on the previous marks.
A1: $T=\frac{2000-448-140}{28}=50.4$. Or better (50.42857...). Accept 50.

questions.stem:
Two particles $P$ and $Q$, of mass 2 kg and 3 kg respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string. Initially $P$ is held at rest on a fixed smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The string passes over a small smooth fixed pulley at the top of the plane. The particle $Q$ hangs freely below the pulley and 0.6 m above the ground, as shown in Figure 3. The part of the string from $P$ to the pulley is parallel to a line of greatest slope of the plane. The system is released from rest with the string taut.

For the motion before $Q$ hits the ground,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) (i) show that the acceleration of $Q$ is $\frac{2g}{5}$,
(ii) find the tension in the string.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Eqn of motion for $Q$: must have the correct terms but condone sign errors.
A1: Correct equation: $3g-T=3a$.
M1: Eqn of motion for $P$: must have the correct terms but condone sign errors. Weight must be resolved.
A1: Correct equation: $T-2g\cos60=2a$ ($T-g=2a$).
Allow M1A1 for $3g-2g\cos60=5a$ in place of either of these two equations.
DM1: Use an exact method to solve for $a$ (i.e. not the equation solver on their calculator). Dependent on the first 2 M marks or the M for the combined equation: $2g=5a$.
A1: $a=\frac{2g}{5}$ * Given answer derived correctly from exact working.
M1: Use given acceleration to solve for $T$: $T=2\times\frac{2g}{5}+g=\frac{9g}{5}$.
A1: accept 18 or 17.6

parts.label: b
parts.text:
On hitting the ground $Q$ is immediately brought to rest by the impact.

(b) Find the speed of $P$ at the instant when $Q$ hits the ground.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Use the given acceleration to find the speed: $v^2=2\times\frac{2g}{5}\times0.6=\frac{2.4g}{5}$.
A1: $v=\frac{2}{5}\sqrt{3g}$ oe involving $g$. Accept 2.2 or 2.17

parts.label: c
parts.text:
In its subsequent motion $P$ does not reach the pulley.

(c) Find the total distance moved up the plane by $P$ before it comes to instantaneous rest.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) B1: String slack: accel of $P$ (up plane) $=-g\cos60=-\frac{1}{2}g$.
M1: Use of $v^2=u^2+2as$ or equivalent for their acceleration $\neq\frac{2g}{5}$: $0=\frac{2.4g}{5}-gs$.
A1: $s=\frac{2.4g}{5}\times\frac{1}{g}=\frac{2.4}{5}=0.48$.
A1ft: Total dist $=1.08$ m. $0.6+$ their 0.48.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Find the length of time between $Q$ hitting the ground and $P$ first coming to instantaneous rest.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: Use of $v=u+at$ or equivalent with their acceleration $\neq\frac{2g}{5}$ to find $t$: $0=\frac{2}{5}\sqrt{3g}-\frac{g}{2}t$ ($0=2.17-4.9t$).
A1: $t=\frac{4\sqrt{3g}}{5g}=0.4426...=0.44$ or 0.443 only
